title: Generate Parentheses
description: Build all valid parenthesis combinations by tracking open and close counts as pruning constraints.

data.text: Given `n` pairs of parentheses, write a function to generate all combinations of well-formed parentheses. A string is well-formed when every `(` has a matching `)` and they are correctly nested.

Build the string character by character, tracking how many `(` and `)` have been used. Add an `(` if we haven't used all `n`; add a `)` only if it wouldn't exceed the number of open `(` (this is the key constraint that guarantees validity). When the string reaches length `2n`, record it. The constraints prune invalid branches automatically, so no generated string is ever malformed.

data.title: Backtracking with open/close counts

data.caption: Decision tree for n=2. A closing is only added when it won't exceed the open count, so every leaf is valid.
data.definition:
graph TB
    A[open=0 close=0] --> B[(]
    B --> C[(]
    C --> D[(() ) => (())]
    B --> E[()]
    E --> F[()()]
    A -.->|close>open not allowed| X[pruned]
    style D fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#2e7d32
    style F fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#2e7d32

data.title: Why the Catalan number shows up
data.text: The count of valid parentheses strings for n pairs is the Catalan number C_n = (2n)! / ((n+1)! * n!). For n=3 that's 5, n=4 is 14. The backtracking constraints prune the tree to exactly these valid strings — it never generates an invalid one and discards it; it simply never builds one.
